name: Cutting garlic and onion

lead: Some people skip garlic and onion to keep breath and skin odour clean. Garlic breath comes mainly from volatile sulfur compounds, especially allyl methyl sulfide, which can persist for up to two days.

Allicin breaks down into allyl methyl sulfide, which is absorbed into the blood and released through the lungs, kidneys and skin. That is why mouthwash and mints are described as not particularly effective. Research measures the compounds and some countermeasures, not avoidance for social outcomes.

paras: People leave garlic and onion out of meals, especially in the day or two before social events, dates or interviews. Some read labels for hidden garlic and onion powders in sauces and seasonings.
No risks are documented in the sources consulted. The main trade-off is dropping common flavouring ingredients from your cooking.

chain: Fewer sulfur compounds in breath and skin
angle.text: Users skip garlic and onion so fewer sulfur compounds reach the breath and skin, leaving a cleaner smell. Allyl methyl sulfide is documented in breath and can persist for up to two days; direct trials on body odour are limited.

lead: Cutting garlic and onion is the practice of dropping these foods from the diet to reduce breath and body odor, so that a person smells fresher in close contact. It is used by people who want to remove a common, diet-driven source of odor that brushing and mouthwash do not fully reach.

Garlic's odor arises when allicin breaks down in the stomach and liver into sulfur compounds including allyl methyl sulfide (AMS), allyl mercaptan, diallyl disulfide and methyl mercaptan.[1] AMS breaks down slowly, so its smell can last for hours and up to about two days, and it is absorbed into the bloodstream and excreted through the lungs, kidneys and skin, which is why mouthwash and mints are described as not very effective.[1] Garlic and onion are among foods named as leaving odorous residue in the mouth, with some compounds entering the blood and being exhaled.[2]

Researchers have measured garlic compounds on human skin and tested food-based deodorising, but no study has compared people who avoid garlic and onion with those who do on how others perceive their smell.
infobox: Hours, up to about two days[1]

paras: The practice ranges from skipping garlic and onion before social events to removing them from the diet. Related odor management in appearance communities also covers oral hygiene and tongue cleaning, since oral bacteria are the main source of ordinary bad breath.

Allicin in garlic breaks down into sulfur compounds including AMS, allyl mercaptan, diallyl disulfide and methyl mercaptan.[1] AMS is the slowest to break down and is carried by the blood to the mouth, lungs, urine and skin, so it is exhaled and secreted in sweat as well as present in the mouth.[1][3] Body odor in general mainly comes from apocrine sweat glands, whose secretions are broken down by skin bacteria, and food, drink, the gut microbiome and genetics can influence it; in one skin analysis men who ate more fruit and vegetables had sweat judged more pleasant.[4]

Halitosis itself is most often oral: about 85 to 90 percent of genuine cases arise from bacteria on the back of the tongue and other oral sources, with foods such as garlic, onion, meat, fish, cheese and cabbage leaving residue that can persist.[2] Encyclopedic sources add that dietary changes and chewing gum are not supported as reliable fixes for halitosis overall.[2]

A 2020 Scientific Reports study by Sato and colleagues measured diallyl disulfide and AMS emanating from the human skin surface and the influence of eating grilled garlic.[3] A 2024 Applied Sciences paper by Hiramoto and colleagues reported that eating natural food additives containing phenolic compounds and polyphenol oxidase reduced the release of AMS from the body.[3]

An Ohio State University study (2010) found milk reduced garlic breath, and a study reported by BBC Future rated lettuce, chicory, celery, potato, parsley, mint, peppermint and basil among the best remedies, with raw foods working better because the degrading enzymes are heat-sensitive.[1]

Small human studies have measured garlic-derived compounds on skin and in breath, and tested foods that reduce them, as above.[1][3] Studies of eliminating garlic and onion to change how others perceive body odor were not found.
